entries.title: Console wolf status filtering: busy wolves are reachable
entries.summary: Console code that selects a wolf to talk to must exclude only wolves with status `offline` (`status !== "offline"`), never require `status === "online"`. A wolf reports `busy` while mid-turn and must still serve the Work API, graduation and live activity; otherwise features fail intermittently when the user's only wolf (1uk4) is working.

entries.title: Plaintext API Keys in Local Wolf Session Logs
entries.summary: Local wolf session logs under `~/wolves/local/<wolf>/agent/sessions/` record all tool output, so an environment dump run in a session writes every secret in the environment to the log in plaintext. One known case is a 1uk4 session log whose keys must be rotated and the file cleaned. Content copied into the shared knowledge base should be secret-scanned first.

entries.title: Subagent Pane vs Background Spawn Behavior
entries.summary: wolfpack-subagents decides whether a spawned subagent opens in a new Herdr pane or runs as a background child process with `effectivePane = (params.pane ?? agentDefs.pane ?? false) && isMuxAvailable()`. An explicit `pane` argument from the orchestrator overrides the agent profile's `pane` setting, multiplexer availability is checked once per process and cached, and the orchestrator instructions say the default comes from each agent's own setting as shown in `subagents_list`.

entries.title: Thread composer images and dictation
entries.summary: The wolf thread composer accepts images by paste, drop or file picker, uploading them to the wolf's worker so the wolf sees them directly, and hosts the Deepgram dictation bar plus inline mics on prose fields.

entries.title: Hal Personal Assistant Features
entries.summary: Hal is a personal assistant wolf (pi-durable, Telegram bot @wolfpack_hal_bot) with five planned features: Morning Briefing, Day Planner, Sunday Fitness Review, Gym-Log Bridge and Natural Language Task Creation. Only the Gym-Log Bridge works. The Day Planner was built on 2026-10-15 but never worked; it was moved out of core to `examples/extensions/planner`.

entries.title: claude-stateless provider: install, dependency and operating notes
entries.summary: claude-stateless is a stateless variant of the owner's pi-claude-bridge fork, installed alongside the default parked-mode bridge. Each round rebuilds a fresh session from thread history and resumes it for one reply, then exits instead of keeping a parked query alive, avoiding the 50-turn cap and parked-process bugs. Its dependency is a local git+file ref that must become a pushed github ref before any VPS deploy. Wolf 1uk4 runs its smart tier on it.

entries.title: Console chat header git row (ThreadGitRow)
entries.summary: The console chat header has two rows. Row 1 keeps the usual TopBar content; row 2, ThreadGitRow (28px), shows the thread workspace's git state as repo · base → branch chips, a worktree badge and dirty/ahead counts, and opens a popover with details. It renders nothing when the thread has no git workspace.

entries.title: Interaction cards and structured output feature plan (J1l2rmD)
entries.summary: Feature J1l2rmD in the wolfpack console covers interaction cards, a needs-you list, structured objects, image upload and dictation. The spec (30 user stories, from four grilling rounds and 24 questions) is approved, and the plan is 15 end-to-end tickets, each sized for one fresh context.

entries.title: Orchestrator main agent and the lean subagent roster
entries.summary: On pi CLI wolves (1uk4) the main agent acts as an orchestrator: it keeps the conversation with the user and delegates whenever only a conclusion, not raw tool output, is needed. Delegation goes through the `wolfpack-subagents` extension to a small roster of agents, each pinned to a model tier. pi-durable wolves do not have subagents yet.

entries.title: CLI command structure and dual-audience design
entries.summary: The `wolfpack` CLI (`packages/cli/src/bin/wolfpack.ts`) was cut from about 22 commands to a short primary set. Every command works two ways: a wizard for humans and flags for scripts and LLM tool calls, backed by the same code. Rarely used operations are folded into wizards or run automatically. Model tiers and transport are configured here too; the full model configuration design is in kb-wolfpack-tK2SB8f.

entries.title: Discord & MCP Integration (Claude Code tooling)
entries.summary: How the owner's Claude Code sessions reach the Snapjack Discord server through an MCP server, plus the bot behind the invite link and the related Telegram MCP workaround. This is a record of the setup as of April 2026, not of anything in the wolfpack codebase; the Snapjack product itself is documented in the snapjack domain.

entries.title: Console Polish, Feature Management and App Follow-ups Work Structure
entries.summary: State of the wolfpack work plan around console UI refinements, feature management and post-cutover app follow-ups: which items are shipped, deferred or archived, the rule for graduating a feature, what stays open, and cleanup decisions.

entries.title: Subagents as durable child conversations
entries.summary: On wolfd, subagents are task-owned durable child conversations spawned by a home or feature thread. A child starts fresh with only its brief, records no memory observations, cannot bind or spawn, and returns results and questions to its parent as steer messages. Running subagents are capped at 3 per wolf and 6 per host with overflow queued, and the console shows children in a status strip, nested in the sidebar, in a Job panel and in a subagent modal.

entries.title: Feature threads and worktree isolation for subagents
entries.summary: A feature thread is a peer of a wolf's home thread, bound to one feature and behaving like home. Writing subagents spawned in a git repo get their own branch and worktree by default; shipping a task rebases and fast-forwards the child branch into the feature branch and removes the worktree. A guard refuses a second unisolated writer in the same working directory, and merging the feature into main stays manual.

entries.title: Console Subagent panel and switchable right panel
entries.summary: The console's right side is a panel host that switches between panels. It holds the Memory panel and a Subagent panel that shows a child's transcript, a ledger of messages and a steer field, opened from the status strip or sidebar without leaving the parent thread.

entries.title: wolfpack-telegram (pi extension): headless auto-connect bridge
entries.summary: `extensions/wolfpack-telegram/` is the Telegram integration for the pi runtime. It is a thin adaptation of badlogic/pi-telegram (MIT) for wolves that run `pi --mode rpc` with no TUI, and it still serves local TUI wolves. It is a different code path from the grammY bot that runs inside the pi-durable harness (`packages/harness/src/telegram/`, see [[kb-wolfpack-PZyLRVg]]); VPS wolves on pi-durable use the harness bot, not this bridge.

entries.title: Telegram voice transcription: agent /transcribe endpoint and whisper.cpp
entries.summary: Voice notes sent to a wolf's Telegram bot are transcribed by a shared speech-to-text endpoint on the wolfpack agent, which runs whisper.cpp. The bot side is described in [[kb-wolfpack-PZyLRVg]].

entries.title: wolfpack-telegram: Architecture and Message Flow
entries.summary: How Telegram is integrated in pi-durable wolf harnesses: a grammY bot running inside the harness process, a tool extension that gives the model buttons, keyboards, reactions, attachments and message management, and the shared state joining the two. Voice transcription is in [[kb-wolfpack-PX7Pnmp]]. The older `pi --mode rpc` bridge (`extensions/wolfpack-telegram/index.ts`) is a different component.

entries.title: Composer per-thread settings: model tier dropdown and auto-ship toggle
entries.summary: The console thread composer has two per-thread controls: a model tier dropdown (main / smart / fast, resolved via models.json) and an auto-ship toggle (off by default for new threads). Settings are persisted per thread through wolfd settings routes (GET/PUT /v1/threads/:id/settings), survive restarts including on the home thread, and feed the task ship policy, where a wolf-wide env var and the tasks config take precedence over the thread flag.

entries.title: Interaction cards in the wolf thread view
entries.summary: Wolves ask the operator questions through inline cards in the Wolfpack Console thread view. A card holds one or more fields (free-text, single, multi, confirm) with optional defaults that only pre-select. A card ends the turn, marks the thread needs-you, waits indefinitely, and the answer starts the next turn. Tools such as task_done and the crawl flow raise cards themselves.

entries.title: Dockerize Wolfpack Initiative (Archived): 9-Component Restructure
entries.summary: The Dockerize Wolfpack initiative (work item `u0wVNj1`) is archived. It planned to containerize wolves, the shared agent and the Tailscale layer, but was superseded by a CLI-only, local-first host setup in which hosts are optional for 24/7 operation. This entry records the last design (9 components) for reference.

entries.title: Wolfpack Console app scaffold (console, desktop and client packages)
entries.summary: The Wolfpack Console front end is a Turbo monorepo on the console branch with two apps, `@wolfpack/console` (Next.js, lifted from learnharness) and `@wolfpack/desktop` (thin Electron shell), plus `@wolfpack/client`, a mock-backed ConsoleClient seam that later becomes the real SDK. Apps depend on packages/client, never the reverse, and only packages/harness will import pi-durable.

entries.title: Console Chat View and Thread Navigation
entries.summary: The Wolfpack Console chat view is the desktop/web thread screen at /wolf/[name]/thread/[threadId], where a user chats with a wolf with live streaming, steer/abort and reattach. It renders the stored assistant message exactly (live and after reload), shows tool calls and results as grouped, collapsible rows, hides empty thinking blocks, and wraps prose within the column. The Telegram live preview uses the same event mapper as the console.

entries.title: Wolfpack Console Initiative: Features, Milestone 1 and Scaffold
entries.summary: The Wolfpack Console initiative (pi-durable harness and control plane) splits the console into eleven features in build order, plus a subscription-bridge feature, with explicit dependencies. Milestone 1 is a thin vertical slice (features 1, 2, 3 and a minimal 6): chat only, one wolf, no hub. Feature 2, the protocol and client SDK, is the next unblocked feature after the scaffold.

entries.title: wolfd thread prompts: identity, orchestrator rules and wolf env
entries.summary: wolfd builds the prompt for home and feature threads from the wolf's identity file plus the same orchestrator rules the terminal pi injects, while subagent threads keep only their profile prompt. For non-sandbox wolves wolfd also sets WOLF_DEN and WOLF_NAME from the wolf config.

entries.title: Multi-ship confirmation card for task_done
entries.summary: task_done (extensions/wolfpack-memory/unified-tasks.ts) accepts several task ids and asks one multi-select confirmation card instead of one card per task. A single id keeps the yes/no card. Per-id checks against the answered card decide which tasks ship, and parallel task_done calls fold into one question.

entries.title: Kitty Graphics in Pi TUI via Herdr: Configuration Guide
entries.summary: Enabling kitty terminal graphics protocol for the pi TUI when running inside a Herdr multiplexer requires two explicit config changes: `experimental.kitty_graphics=true` in Herdr and `terminal.images=kitty` in wolf settings.json, because Herdr resets TERM to xterm-256color, breaking pi's auto-detection.

entries.title: Card-answer silent turn hang
entries.summary: Answering an interaction card (ask_user_question or a task_done ship card) sometimes does not produce the assistant's next output, leaving the thread on a working spinner. Session-store evidence shows follow-up turns that started but whose model call produced nothing, with no watchdog in wolfd to abort or surface them. The likely root cause is the old pi-claude-bridge provider keeping tool calls parked between turns; the claude-stateless provider did not reproduce it in testing. A silent-turn watchdog and related fixes remain planned.

entries.title: Open-source readiness: lean repo + docs
entries.summary: The initiative makes the repo lean, free of owner-specific content and documented for open-source release. It is complete once its five child features and the local-first feature ship and gitleaks is clean. It is open and paused: the owner put the local-hosting, hub and Dewey-fix work on hold on 2026-10-21; changes already on main stay and nothing is deployed for it.

entries.title: Wolfpack Console repo docs policy and branch hygiene
entries.summary: On the console branch, repo docs hold distilled current truth and move with code in the same commit, while work items keep full history. Only main and console remain on GitHub; old branches are archived as local tags.

entries.title: Cutover of 1uk4 to the app (option X)
entries.summary: 1uk4 now runs in the app under workerd with live memory, carrying the former sandbox den, threads and history; the terminal pi 1uk4 is retired. The cutover made the sandbox ledger and work items live on sfo-01 using reviewed cutover and rollback scripts.

entries.title: Work item scheduling
entries.summary: A work item can be pinned to a calendar slot with two nullable fields: `scheduledFor` (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`, local time, no timezone) and `durationMinutes` (a positive integer). Without a duration the item is a timeline dot; with one it is a calendar block. Scheduling is a ledger event, so it is part of an item's history and reaches every client through the Work API ([[kb-wolfpack-fT2y8XM]]).

entries.title: Live work Record for bound work items
entries.summary: While a work item is bound, agent observations carry the item's id, are routed to its feature Record instead of den topics, and never reach the den or KB except through graduation. Each bound item's working document has a curated `## Record` section that is rewritten as things change, and the plan plus Record are injected into agent context.

entries.title: Sub-agent worktree cleanup and stale Not merged notices
entries.summary: Sub-agents cut from the home checkout rather than a feature branch are not auto-merged and report "Not merged: no feature branch to merge it into"; those notices are stale once their commits are on the wolf branch (wolf/1uk4) or the orchestrator has merged them, and can be ignored. Worktrees live under the wolf's workspaces directory as feat-home--<name> and are removed after confirming the branch is merged and clean.

entries.title: Work-item hygiene report (wolfpack work doctor)
entries.summary: Work-item hygiene is a read-only report, run with `wolfpack work doctor [--domain d] [--json]`, that lists stale, contradicted and shipped-not-graduated work items. The owner approves a fix list, and fixes are applied through the Work API. The check is repeatable at any time.

entries.title: Active Task split: stable header and turn-boundary notices
entries.summary: The system prompt's Active Task section carries only a stable header, and changes to the bound item reach the model as short user-turn notices at turn boundaries. The full working document is read through task_current. This works identically on every transport.

entries.title: Work Item Dependency System
entries.summary: How work items depend on each other: schema, validity rules, blocking logic, the `/task` selector controls and the dashboard graph. The selector as a whole is in [[kb-wolfpack-5T2V5AY]]; the dashboard's Work view is in [[kb-wolfpack-dPCp03V]].

entries.title: Work Item Visual System — Kind-Based Icons & Graph Colors
entries.summary: Defines the canonical icon, emoji, color, and display logic for work items across the /task dashboard and KB graph, replacing the old stage-based icon system.

entries.title: Work Dependency Routes on the Knowledge Graph
entries.summary: The console knowledge graph shows how work items depend on each other as routes. Work items sit under a Factory node per domain, and selecting a task or feature highlights its full completion route from the Factory through prerequisite features and tasks, as layered steps with parallel groups. Dependency arrows are drawn faintly only when zoomed into a Factory region, the selected route is drawn bright on top, and the node card steps along the route with arrows and a dropdown at forks and joins.

entries.title: Console Work View: Browsing Work with Graph Route Selection
entries.summary: The Work view is a full overlay in the Wolfpack Console, opened from a Work button in the graph header or a Work entry in the sidebar nav. It lists a domain's work as Inbox/initiative groups, feature rows and task rows with sortable columns, search and a graduated toggle. Dependencies show as left-gutter connectors. Selecting a row splits the screen: a resizable left table beside the graph, which draws that item's route.

entries.title: Console knowledge graph with Factory nodes
entries.summary: The console's knowledge graph draws only the structural hierarchy, with no relation links between entries. Each domain gets a Factory node with that domain's work items attached beneath it, as on the KB website.

entries.title: Factory task system: WorkItem design
entries.summary: The Factory is the work layer that sits between raw work sessions and the graduated KB library. A WorkItem is an event-sourced record with a tree position (what it is part of) and an area (what kind of work it is). The schema, events, fold and rules are in `packages/kb/src/schema/work.ts`; storage is served by the Work API ([[kb-wolfpack-fT2y8XM]]); the agent-facing tools are in [[kb-wolfpack-9beRX8B]] and the interactive UI in [[kb-wolfpack-5T2V5AY]].

entries.title: Console feature progress panel and thread binding
entries.summary: A thread bound to a work item shows a collapsible pinned graph of its feature at the top of the console chat, built live from the Work API, with one column per route layer. Threads are bound to items through POST /v1/threads/:id/bind, which enforces several refusal rules.

entries.title: Structured agent output objects
entries.summary: Wolves show their work as live structured objects in the thread: decision, checklist and graph cards. They are carried by an additive `object-upsert` event, update in place with an "updated N times" marker, and survive reload. A pinned checklist shows progress at the top of the thread.

entries.title: KB graduation routing and structure hardening
entries.summary: A review of the first 14 live KB writes from local-first and Work-items-KB graduations found correct format and anchors but 2 misroutes (a duplicate sweep entry and a cross-domain alias bug), oversized multi-subject entries, a missing Delivered list and a section tree that does not follow subjects. Fixes for routing, size handling, linting and stale-build detection are live; the section-tree review and KB corrections remain open.

entries.title: KB Frontmatter Corruption: Root Causes, Fixes & Migration
entries.summary: Why KB frontmatter corrupted (LLM-ordered serialization, free-form type, no post-LLM validation), the deterministic renderer, controlled kinds and referential-integrity gate that replaced it, and how knowledge reaches wolves.

entries.title: KB reorg rebuild and sweep operational behavior
entries.summary: Operational notes for running `kb_reorg rebuild=true`, `kb_sweep`, entry retirement and snapjack shard-splitting: rebuilds re-cluster the section tree but are non-deterministic and non-converging, so run one per batch of new entries and confirm scope when a request is ambiguous.

entries.title: Work graduation: distilled contributions, anchored initiative entries, link-back
entries.summary: Graduating a finished feature (or a loose Inbox task) turns its plan, Record and Outcomes into ordinary KB contributions through the same distill step as den topics. The owner confirms a preview, Dewey's sweep routes each contribution like any other, and one anchored entry per initiative gives an overview. A shipped item gets no entry of its own: its knowledge merges into the subject entries it concerns, and the item is cited only at the end of History lines.

entries.title: KB Section Tree Algorithm: Bottom-Up Agglomerative Clustering
entries.summary: The algorithm that builds and maintains a domain's KB section tree: bottom-up agglomerative clustering for full rebuilds, recursive descent for incremental placement, abstraction scoring by entry kind, and drift-based relabeling. It replaced a top-down k-means that produced weight inversions and singleton roots. Implementation and maintenance are in [[kb-wolfpack-Wq5Pkio]]; rebuild-safety invariants in [[kb-wolfpack-foy1o3U]].

entries.title: KB section tree: implementation, reorg pipeline and maintenance
entries.summary: How the KB section tree is built and kept healthy: the unified reorg pipeline (rebuild phases and incremental path), placement domain filtering, the reorg CLI, tuning parameters and the open post-absorb split gap.

entries.title: KB rebuild-safety invariants: orphan prevention, one-writer lock, titles
entries.summary: Rules that keep the KB section tree consistent while sections are created, merged and deleted, and while a sweep and a reorg run at the same time. They live in `packages/kb/src/librarian/reorg.ts` and `lock.ts`. The algorithm is in [[kb-wolfpack-VB1Io8T]] and the reorg pipeline in [[kb-wolfpack-Wq5Pkio]].

entries.title: Standing feature graduation to pinned KB entries
entries.summary: Features under a standing initiative (for example weekly Fitness or Daily Planning; standing is a manual user decision) graduate to their own anchored, verbatim KB entry instead of being condensed. The initiative's entry holds live current state plus a code-built Delivered list linking each feature entry. Reorg keeps feature entries beside the holder, and retire refuses anchored entries without --force. Ordinary features graduate as before.

entries.title: KB History Model
entries.summary: KB entries are a regenerable view over an immutable record (contributions, decisions, versions). Each entry states current truth and keeps replaced facts as labelled history in a ## History section; decisions are immutable and superseded rather than edited; previous copies are saved under versions/ without git. The den keeps the raw event record, the KB keeps durable state.

entries.title: Solo Session Recorder Redesign — Mobile UI, Testing Policy & Risks
entries.summary: Archived 2026-07-20 plan covering mobile pure modules, UI tasks (8–16), TimeWheel extraction, testing policy, legacy risks, and implementation context.

entries.title: Onboarding Funnels — Analytics, Event Gaps, and Decision Log
entries.summary: Covers PostHog wiring, the 28-event taxonomy, the stakes.completed under-fire gap, commit history, and the full decision log.

entries.title: Stats: Analytics Dashboard UI & Admin Tooling
entries.summary: Covers the analytics dashboard structure, filters, key UI components, UX patterns, admin diagnostics, and the proposed Poker Wrapped feature.

entries.title: Game Tracking — Architecture, Data Models & Algorithms
entries.summary: Game tracking as of 2026-08-30: Game document with an embedded events[] log and write-time PlayerStats, Game and AdminAdjustment models, GameRevision as an admin-adjustment audit record (not the event log), core algorithms, permissions, privacy, performance.

entries.title: Stats: API Routes, PlayerStats Model & Statistics Engine
entries.summary: Covers the 10 API routes, PlayerStats model structure, and the multiplayer statistics engine including computed metrics, bucket analysis, and caching.

entries.title: Development Timeline (March–September 2026)
entries.summary: Month-by-month engineering timeline from March 24 through September 29, 2026, covering game management redesigns, league systems, onboarding flows, invitation unification, admin portal rebuild, solo session tracking, and marketing tooling.

entries.title: WinningsChart Mobile Implementation Plan — Victory-Native Cumulative Profit Line + Monthly Bars
entries.summary: 2026-03-26 plan to add a cumulative profit line chart with monthly summary bars to the mobile Activity tab, using victory-native and existing `/api/analytics/poker/winnings-over-time` endpoint. Chart placed above stats cards with independent 1M/3M/6M/12M period pills, smart point selection (max 80 points), and separate bar row rendering. No API or PlayerStats model changes required.

entries.title: Onboarding Funnels — Flows, Naming, Packages, and Analytics
entries.summary: Covers the naming collision between intro and league funnels, Phase A/B intro flow details, league onboarding, signup-claim flow, and all shared packages.

entries.title: Stats: PostHog Instrumentation & Mobile Event Tracking
entries.summary: Covers PostHog ingest proxy setup, client-side filtering, mobile lifecycle events, and the league onboarding analytics event family.

grabBag.title: Mobile PokerNow Import Wizard — Atomic Settlement Design
grabBag.summary: Archived 2026-06-07 design for mobile 3-screen PokerNow import wizard with atomic import-and-settle flow, backed by refactored settlement math and idempotent confirm route landing completed games.

grabBag.title: MOC Visual Refresh — Design Inspiration Collection
grabBag.summary: Seedling-stage inspiration collection for the Snapjack MOC visual refresh, anchored by a Dribbble crypto poker UI reference featuring a dark theme, card animations, chip styling, and clean table layout.

grabBag.title: Unified Invitation Token Design – Implementation Tasks 1–8 (2026-05-12, Archived)
grabBag.summary: Archived 2026-05-12 eight-task implementation plan covering schema, helper, friend create, search, read, accept, share endpoints, and web render for unified invite tokens.

grabBag.title: Snapjack REST API Reference (route inventory from 2026-04-03; counts re-verified 2026-10-22)
grabBag.summary: Snapjack REST API served at https://snapjack.app/api with source at apps/web/src/app/api/. Counted from the repo on 2026-10-22: 223 `route.ts` files, 81 of them under `admin/` and 142 elsewhere. Earlier sources disagreed (about 190 on 2026-04-03, 216 on 2026-08-30, 220 on 2026-09-07); those were point-in-time counts. The endpoint lists below are the 2026-04-03 inventory.

grabBag.title: Settlements — Strategies, API Routes, and Admin Escape Hatches
grabBag.summary: Covers the four debt-resolution strategies, full REST API surface for settlements and transactions, admin force-complete routes, and error codes.

grabBag.title: Snapjack Monorepo Architecture and API Split Plan
grabBag.summary: Architecture map of the Snapjack monorepo: apps/web is the hub serving the API, admin, legacy dashboard and cron on Vercel. Covers backend boundary findings (most routes bypass services), the recommended domain-by-domain refactor (Option C), and the staged plan to split the API into apps/api while staying on Vercel.

grabBag.title: Solo Session Recorder Redesign — Goals, Problems, Schema & API Plan
grabBag.summary: Archived 2026-07-20 spec covering goals, defects fixed, hourly semantics, and schema/API tasks (1–7) for the solo session recorder redesign.

grabBag.title: iOS System & Subscriptions API (as of 2026-04-04)
grabBag.summary: iOS mobile app lifecycle system (EAS builds, TestFlight, App Store) plus a RevenueCat-backed Subscriptions API covering /api/subscription/*, /api/webhooks/revenuecat/*, and /api/cron/check-receipts/*. Documented 2026-04-04; the four route files still exist as of 2026-10-22. The paywall's current rules live in kb-snapjack-H5nYJ6a.

grabBag.title: Notifications — Event Types, Deep Links, Analytics Caveats, Bugs & Changelog
grabBag.summary: Covers all notification event types with copy and triggers, deep link rules, analytics caveats, known bugs including the Vercel push outage, and the full dated changelog.

grabBag.title: Admin Game Details Dialog & Hub Consolidation
grabBag.summary: Admin-only in-place game details dialog via GET /api/admin/games/[gameId], consolidating Activity and Games tabs into 4-tab hub; includes league card, payment status badges, settlements list, and coarse timeline.

grabBag.title: VPS Max transport via Agent SDK (memory, consolidation, sweep)
grabBag.summary: VPS pi-durable wolves can run their engine steps (memory observation, consolidation, KB sweep and other KB operations) on a Claude Max subscription through the Claude Agent SDK. The pi-durable main agent stays on the metered API key: there is no Max provider for it yet (Phase 2, not built). Mixed mode is supported, so one wolf can be on subscription while another stays on the API.

grabBag.title: KB sweep scheduling, resilience and hardening
grabBag.summary: The KB sweep is the librarian process that merges inbox contributions into the knowledge base. One shared tick, `runSweepTick`, drives it from the pi-durable harness timer on the VPS (no systemd) or from launchd on a Mac, processing the single oldest contribution per 1-minute tick with a 600s item budget. It backs off on infrastructure outages, alerts through Telegram on pause and recovery, parks items it cannot classify, and guards its lock, ledger and inbox. Pipeline stages, merge band and parking detail are in [[kb-wolfpack-is2MGai]].

grabBag.title: guarded_bash read-only guard and the sfo-01 /dev/null incident
grabBag.summary: Read-only subagents get a `guarded_bash` tool that refuses any command that writes, deletes or changes state, including inside `ssh '...'`, `bash -c`, `sudo`, `$(...)`, `xargs` and `find -exec`. It exists because an investigator subagent, told to be read-only but running as root on sfo-01, deleted `/dev/null` and broke SSH on the host for about 38 minutes. The lesson: a read-only instruction to a root subagent is not enforcement. Tool-level guards plus a non-root account are.

grabBag.title: Task UI Overhaul: Two-Pane Workspace Browser
grabBag.summary: `/task` is a keyboard-first, hjkl-navigated two-pane workspace browser over the full hierarchy (initiatives, features, tasks). Only tasks, issues and spikes are agent-bindable; features and initiatives are workspace-level. The panel lives in `extensions/wolfpack-memory/work-system.ts`; the pure selector/reducer is `packages/memory/src/work/selector.ts`. The agent works the same data through `task_create`, `task_done`, `task_note`, `task_move`, `task_link` and `task_unlink`.
